**Question 2.** Which groups of countries share similar electricity-generation mixes?

This document uses the prepared data from Part 1 (render `01_data_preparation_eda.Rmd` first). The
Python version is `python/03_q2_clustering.ipynb`.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
# ---- Setup ----
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(cluster)

theme_set(theme_minimal())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5)

df <- read.csv("../data/processed/power_plants_clean_r.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
dim(df)
```

# 1. Approach

The approach mirrors the Python version: each country with at least 1 GW of capacity is described by
the share of its capacity in eight fuel groups (Coal, Gas, Oil, Hydro, Nuclear, Wind, Solar, Other).
**k-means** (50 random starts) is run on these shares, which are already on a common 0–1 scale; k is
chosen with the elbow and silhouette methods; and **hierarchical clustering** (Ward linkage) is compared
using the adjusted Rand index.

```{r shares}
fuels <- c("Coal", "Gas", "Oil", "Hydro", "Nuclear", "Wind", "Solar", "Other")
cap <- df %>%
  mutate(mix = ifelse(primary_fuel == "Nuclear", "Nuclear", fuel)) %>%
  group_by(country_long, mix) %>%
  summarise(mw = sum(capacity_mw), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = mix, values_from = mw, values_fill = 0)
cap$total <- rowSums(cap[fuels])
big <- cap %>% filter(total >= 1000)
shares <- as.matrix(big[fuels] / big$total)
rownames(shares) <- big$country_long
cat("Countries with at least 1 GW:", nrow(shares), "of", nrow(cap), "\n")
round(apply(shares, 2, quantile, probs = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)), 3)
```

# 2. Choosing the number of clusters

```{r choose-k, fig.height = 4}
set.seed(42)
ks <- 2:10
k_stats <- do.call(rbind, lapply(ks, function(k) {
  km <- kmeans(shares, centers = k, nstart = 50, iter.max = 100)
  sil <- silhouette(km$cluster, dist(shares))
  data.frame(k = k, inertia = km$tot.withinss, silhouette = mean(sil[, "sil_width"]))
}))

ggplot(k_stats, aes(k, inertia)) + geom_line(colour = "steelblue") + geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Elbow Method", x = "Number of clusters (k)", y = "Within-cluster sum of squares")
ggplot(k_stats, aes(k, silhouette)) + geom_line(colour = "darkorange") + geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Silhouette Score", x = "Number of clusters (k)", y = "Mean silhouette width")
round(k_stats, 3)
```

**Interpretation.** The silhouette score is `r round(k_stats$silhouette[k_stats$k == 4], 3)` at k = 4 and
`r round(k_stats$silhouette[k_stats$k == 5], 3)` at k = 5, essentially equal, and the elbow flattens
around these values. As in Python, k = 5 is used because it also separates the oil-dominated countries.

# 3. The clusters

```{r clusters}
set.seed(42)
K <- 5
km <- kmeans(shares, centers = K, nstart = 50, iter.max = 100)

name_cluster <- function(row) {
  top <- sort(row, decreasing = TRUE)
  if (top[1] >= 0.5) return(paste0(names(top)[1], "-dominated"))
  if (top[1] < 0.3) return("Diversified")
  paste(names(top)[1], "and", names(top)[2])
}
profile <- aggregate(as.data.frame(shares), list(cluster = km$cluster), mean)
cluster_names <- apply(profile[fuels], 1, name_cluster)
labels <- cluster_names[km$cluster]
names(labels) <- rownames(shares)

profile_table <- data.frame(cluster = cluster_names, round(profile[fuels], 2),
                            countries = as.vector(table(km$cluster)),
                            total_GW = round(tapply(big$total, km$cluster, sum) / 1000))
profile_table
```

```{r heatmap, fig.height = 4}
heat <- profile_table %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(cluster, " (", countries, ")")) %>%
  select(label, all_of(fuels)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-label, names_to = "fuel", values_to = "share")
ggplot(heat, aes(factor(fuel, levels = fuels), label, fill = share)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", share)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "lightyellow", high = "firebrick") +
  labs(title = "Average Capacity Mix of Each Cluster", x = "Fuel",
       y = "Cluster (number of countries)", fill = "Mean share")
```

```{r members}
members <- data.frame(country = rownames(shares), cluster = labels,
                      GW = round(big$total / 1000)) %>%
  arrange(cluster, desc(GW))
for (cl in sort(unique(members$cluster))) {
  m <- members$country[members$cluster == cl]
  cat(sprintf("%s (%d): %s%s\n", cl, length(m), paste(head(m, 15), collapse = ", "),
              ifelse(length(m) > 15, " ...", "")))
}
```

```{r pca, fig.height = 6}
pca <- prcomp(shares)
coords <- data.frame(pca$x[, 1:2], cluster = labels, country = rownames(shares))
var_pct <- round(100 * pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2))
show <- c("China", "United States of America", "India", "Brazil", "France", "Germany",
          "Saudi Arabia", "Russia", "Canada", "Norway", "Spain", "Japan")
ggplot(coords, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = cluster)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_text(data = subset(coords, country %in% show),
            aes(label = sub("United States of America", "USA", country)),
            size = 2.8, vjust = -0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Countries by Generation Mix (first two principal components)",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", var_pct[1], "% of variance)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", var_pct[2], "% of variance)"), colour = "Cluster")
```

# 4. Checking the clusters

```{r checks}
sil <- silhouette(km$cluster, dist(shares))
sil_by <- data.frame(cluster = labels, width = sil[, "sil_width"]) %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  summarise(mean = round(mean(width), 3), min = round(min(width), 3), size = n())
sil_by

# Hierarchical clustering with Ward linkage and the same k
hc <- cutree(hclust(dist(shares), method = "ward.D2"), k = K)

adjusted_rand <- function(a, b) {
  tab <- table(a, b)
  comb2 <- function(x) sum(choose(x, 2))
  index <- comb2(tab)
  expected <- comb2(rowSums(tab)) * comb2(colSums(tab)) / choose(sum(tab), 2)
  max_index <- (comb2(rowSums(tab)) + comb2(colSums(tab))) / 2
  (index - expected) / (max_index - expected)
}
ari <- adjusted_rand(km$cluster, hc)
cat(sprintf("Adjusted Rand index, k-means vs hierarchical: %.3f\n", ari))
table(kmeans = labels, hierarchical = hc)
```

```{r save}
write.csv(members, "../report/figures/q2_country_clusters_r.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(profile_table, "../report/figures/q2_cluster_profiles_r.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# 5. Discussion

R finds the same five groups as Python: **hydro-dominated**
(`r sum(labels == "Hydro-dominated")` countries), **coal-dominated**
(`r sum(labels == "Coal-dominated")`, including China and India), **gas-dominated**
(`r sum(labels == "Gas-dominated")`), **oil-dominated** (`r sum(labels == "Oil-dominated")`) and a
looser **diversified** group (`r sum(labels == "Diversified")`, including the United States, Germany,
Japan and France). The diversified group has the lowest mean silhouette
(`r sil_by$mean[sil_by$cluster == "Diversified"]`), and the adjusted Rand index with hierarchical
clustering is `r sprintf("%.3f", ari)`. 119 of the 120 countries fall in the same cluster as in Python;
the exception, Cote d'Ivoire, sits on the border between the hydro and diversified groups. No group is led by wind or solar, because their capacity shares
are still small in this 2021 snapshot. Shares are of capacity, not generation, and coverage varies by
country.
